correctness.rationale: Tree bridges are series resistors across s(N-s) unordered vertex pairs. Each clique has Laplacian modes n_i b_i and b_i+(n_i-1)a_i, yielding exact local objective (N-n_i+1)/b_i+N(n_i-2)/ell_i and linear budget n_i b_i/2+(n_i-2)ell_i/2. The sharp Cauchy-Schwarz bound reaches H²/B at the displayed positive allocation, with ell_i/b_i=sqrt(N n_i/(N-n_i+1))>1. Strict inverse-trace convexity plus edge-weight injectivity establishes unrestricted uniqueness. Five direct grounded-Laplacian checks, 250 asymmetric feasible perturbations, and five independent all-edge constrained optimizations corroborate the proof, not replace it.

originality.rationale: The inspected closest primary paper handles generic total-resistance optimization, trees and a balanced two-clique barbell. The new exact classification applies simultaneously to arbitrary heterogeneous clique sizes and any one-gateway bridge tree, and adds universal peripheral-contrast spectral equality; neither cited special case states the all-tree formula. Published research-record and literature searches found no equivalent/dominating claim. Residual risk of specialized coverage persists; priority not certified.

value.rationale: Natural complete solution for a heterogeneous community network architecture: exact unrestricted globally optimal edge sizes under one global budget, nontrivial cut-size dependence, and size-independent optimized internal peripheral-contrast eigenvalue across all cliques. Useful benchmark for network robustness and convex conductance design, not merely a numerical table, renaming or tiny parameter increment.
